suggestions.quote: By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
suggestions.fix: Across all sixty-four squares, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).

suggestions.quote: Day fifty-five. The number passes what the whole world makes in a year. Every loaf, every car, every hour of work on Earth. About 128 trillion dollars (c09).
suggestions.fix: Day fifty-five. The number passes what the whole world makes in a year. Every loaf, every car, every hour of work on Earth. About 128 trillion US dollars (c09).

keep.quote: This has happened before. For real. In 1324, a king from Mali, Mansa Musa, gave away so much gold in Cairo that gold stayed cheap there for at least twelve years (c06).
Right here in Berlin, by late 1923, a loaf of bread cost about two hundred billion marks (c01). Anna's board is heading the same way. Give it all away? You hit zero. Berlin doesn't.
Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of hydrogen atoms in the observable universe (c12).
